findings.description: allocate consumes the records iterable twice: once for computing total and again for building the result dictionary. This exhausts one-shot iterators, causing incorrect empty results.
findings.evidence: For example, passing records=iter([("a",1),("b",2)]) to allocate(records, 100) results in an empty dictionary {} instead of {"a":33,"b":66}.

review.summary: The implementation fails to support consuming an iterator only once, violating the contract when records is a generator or other one-shot iterable.
